info.title: Eloverblik.Api.ThirdPartyApi
info.description:
This API enables third parties to access customers' data from DataHub based on authorization (power of attorney) granted by the customer. To gain access to the API the third party must:

  • Be registered as a third party to DataHub.
  • Be authorized by use of a token

You can apply for becoming a third party participant here: https://en.energinet.dk/electricity/new-player/how-to-become-a-third-party/ / Link to danish version: https://energinet.dk/el/elmarkedet/sadan-bliver-du-tredjepart/

Authentication and authorization are handled by using bearer tokens. To get started you need a refresh token. You can generate a refresh token in the ElOverblik portal after logging in with MitID as a registered third party. The token is a long text string (JWT token), which must be copied and stored for use with the system that needs to access the API. When you have obtained a refresh token, you can access the token endpoint to create a short-lived data access token (valid for 24 hours) The data access token allows you to access the rest of the endpoints below.

This API only gives you access to data from active authorizations (powers of attorneys) granted by customers. Data regarding deleted or expired authorizations are not returned.

When requesting user authorizations (powers of attorney) from a third-party application via ElOverblik.dk using a "Power of Attorney" link, it is recommended to follow the technical reference guide for MitID Integration provided by the Signaturgruppen Broker: https://signaturgruppen-a-s.github.io/signaturgruppen-broker-documentation/idps/app-mitid-integration.html

It is possible to set a correlation id in the request header using the 'X-User-Correlation-ID' (with an UUID). When provided this id will follow the request and finally end in the response header. This id can be used for tracking the request. Parallel to this id there is another internally id (Also a UUID), which also is returned in the response header as 'X-Correlation-ID'.

Please be aware that it is only possible to get time series data for the previous 5 years + current year.

Please note: Submission of meter readings to DataHub is no longer mandatory since end of 2021. Therefore, data may not be available for all metering points.

1. Limitations

At times, we may experience higher loads than our underlying data provider, DataHub, can handle. Therefore we have enforced some limitations on the usage of this API:

  • Calls to GetToken are restricted to 2 per minute per IP address.
  • The total number of calls per IP address is restricted to 120 per minute.
  • The total number of calls for all users is restricted to 1200 per minute.

If you exceed any one of these limits, you will get an http error 429 - Too many requests.
If DataHub is not able to keep up with the demand - even if the above limits are not exceeded - you may get an http error 503 - DataHub unavailable.

2. Usage recommendations

  • Bundle requests for 10 metering points at a time.
  • Spread out multiple requests over a longer period.
  • Don't request data for periods of several years repeatedly.
  • If you get an error 429 or 503, wait 1min. before retrying.
  • If you get an error, then try to reduce the amount of metering points or reduce the date period of the request.
  • The data access token is active for 24h and should not need to be refreshed more than once a day.
  • If you get an error or timeout on the /thirdpartyapi/api/authorization/authorization/meteringpoints/ then try to switch to /thirdpartyapi/api/authorization/authorization/meteringpointids/ and then split the meteringpoints into smaller bundles before requesting /thirdpartyapi/api/meteringpoint/getdetails

3. Possible system error codes

General Error Codes

Code Name Description
10000 NoError No error – the operation was successful.
10001 WrongNumberOfArguments The request contains too few or too many arguments. Check the endpoint definition and send exactly the required parameters.

Metering Point

Code Name Description
20000 WrongMeteringPointIdOrWebAccessCode The metering-point ID and web access code could not be validated. Check that both values belong to the same metering point and enter them exactly as issued.
20001 MeteringPointBlocked The metering point is blocked and cannot be linked or queried.
20002 MeteringPointRelationAlreadyExist The metering point is already linked to your account. Use the existing relation instead of creating it again.
20003 MeteringPointIdNot18CharsLong The metering-point ID must contain exactly 18 characters; for example, a 17-digit ID is rejected. Submit the complete ID without leading or trailing spaces.
20004 MeteringpointIdContainsNonDigits The metering-point ID must contain digits only. Remove letters, spaces, hyphens, or other nonnumeric characters.
20005 MeteringPointAliasTooLong The metering-point alias is longer than 50 characters. Shorten the alias and submit it again.
20006 WebAccessCodeNot8CharsLong The web access code must contain exactly 8 characters; for example, a 7- or 9-character code is rejected. Check for missing, extra, or surrounding characters.
20007 WebAccessCodeContainsIllegalChars The web access code may contain letters and digits only. Remove spaces, punctuation, and other symbols.
20008 MeteringPointNotFound No metering point was found for the supplied ID. Check the 18-digit ID and verify that the metering point exists in DataHub.
20009 MeteringPointIsChild The supplied ID identifies a child metering point, which this operation does not support. Use the associated parent metering point.
20010 RelationNotFound Your account has no active relation to the metering point. Obtain authorization before requesting its data.
20011 UnknownError The operation failed because the service received an unexpected error. Retry the request; if it continues to fail, contact support with the correlation ID.
20012 Unauthorized You are not authorized to perform this operation for the metering point. Use a valid access token and ensure that an active authorization exists.
20013 NoValidMeteringPointsInList None of the supplied metering-point IDs is valid. Submit at least one 18-digit ID containing digits only.

MeterData

Code Name Description
30000 FromDateIsGreaterThanToday The start date is in the future; for example, tomorrow is not a valid start date. Set the start date to today or an earlier date.
30001 FromDateIsGreaterThanToDate The start date is later than the end date; for example, a start date of 2026-09-05 cannot be combined with an end date of 2026-09-04. Correct or swap the dates.
30002 ToDateCanNotBeEqualToFromDate The start and end dates are identical. Choose an end date that is later than the start date.
30003 ToDateIsGreaterThanToday The end date is later than tomorrow; for example, a date two days from now is rejected. Set the end date to tomorrow or earlier.
30004 InvalidDateFormat The start date or end date could not be parsed. Send both dates in the documented format, for example 2026-09-04.
30005 InvalidRequestParameters One or more request parameters are missing, malformed, or inconsistent. Check the endpoint's documented scope, identifier, metering-point IDs, dates, and options.
30008 RequestedAggregationUnavaliable The requested aggregation is not supported. Use one of the documented values: Actual, Quarter, Hour, Day, Month, or Year.
30010 DateNotCoveredByAuthorization The authorization does not cover the entire requested period. Limit the dates to the authorization's validity period or obtain a new authorization that covers them.
30011 AggrationNotValid The aggregation value is invalid. Replace it with a supported value listed by the endpoint, such as Hour, Day, or Month.
30014 PeriodNotAllowed The effective end date is not later than the start date. This can happen when dateFrom is today and dateTo is tomorrow, because future end dates are adjusted to today before data is requested. Choose a start date before today or otherwise ensure that the adjusted end date remains later than the start date.
30015 NoDataAvailable No time-series values were found for the requested period. Try a different or shorter period and verify that readings have been reported for the metering point.
30016 RelationHasExpired The authorization relation expired before or during the requested period. Request dates covered by an active relation or obtain a new authorization.
30017 ToDateCutOff The end date is on or before the oldest supported date. Choose a later period within the previous five years plus the current year.
30018 MeteringPointDataNotAvailableForTheRequestedPeriod Data cannot be retrieved for the requested period. Either the entire period is outside the metering point's available-data period, or dateFrom is before the metering point was registered in DataHub. Set dateFrom to the registration date or later and request a period within the available-data period.

Authorization

Code Name Description
40000 InvalidCVR The CVR is invalid. Submit the authenticated business's 8-digit CVR; private users cannot submit a CVR.
40001 InvalidIncludeFutureMeteringPointsRelatedToCVR The request does not specify whether future metering points related to the CVR are included. Send true or false.
40002 InvalidMasterDataFields One or more requested master-data fields are unknown or unsupported. Check the field names and use only fields documented by the endpoint.
40003 InvalidMeteringPointIds The metering-point ID list is missing or contains invalid values. Supply the required list and ensure that every ID contains exactly 18 digits.
40004 InvalidSignature The supplied signature could not be validated. Recreate the signed payload with the required signing key and send the signature without modification.
40005 InvalidSignedByNameId The signer identity is missing or invalid. Include the authenticated signer's name ID in SignedByNameId.
40006 InvalidSignedDate The signing date is invalid. Use today's UTC date, or let the API populate the authenticated signing date.
40007 InvalidSignedText The signed authorization text is missing, empty, or cannot be decoded. Send the complete signed text in the required encoded format.
40008 InvalidThirdPartyId The third-party ID is missing or invalid. Supply the ID of a registered third party.
40009 InvalidFromDate The valid-from date is missing or cannot be parsed. Send a valid date within the period allowed for the authorization.
40010 InvalidToDate The valid-to date is missing or cannot be parsed. Send a valid date after the valid-from date and within the allowed authorization period.
40011 ValidToBeforeValidFrom The valid-to date is earlier than the valid-from date. Correct or swap the dates so the authorization ends after it begins.
40012 ValidToOutOfRange The valid-to or access-expiry date is outside the allowed range. Check the endpoint's date requirements and choose a date within the allowed range.
40013 ValidFromOutOfRange The valid-from date is outside the allowed range. Check the endpoint's date requirements and choose a date within the allowed range.
40014 NoAuthorizationsFound No active authorization was found for the requested customer or metering point. Obtain authorization or check the authorization ID, customer CVR, or customer key.

Token

Code Name Description
50000 WrongTokenType This endpoint requires a refresh token issued for the Third Party API. Use the correct Third Party API refresh token instead of a data-access or Customer API token.
50001 TokenNotValid The refresh token is invalid or inactive. Generate or activate a valid Third Party API refresh token, then request a new data-access token.
50002 ErrorCreatingToken The service could not create a data-access token. Verify that the refresh token is valid and active, then retry; contact support with the correlation ID if the error persists.
50003 TokenRegistrationFailed The refresh token could not be registered. Retry the registration; if it continues to fail, contact support with the correlation ID.
50004 TokenAlreadyActive The refresh token is already active and does not need to be activated again. Use it to request a data-access token, or activate a different inactive token.
50005 TokenAlreadyDeactivaed The refresh token is already inactive and cannot be deactivated again. Activate it before use, or select another active token.

get.description:
This request is used for retrieving a list of metering points for which access has been granted.
A filter value must be supplied to limit the result.
            
The following filter options are available:
            
`authorizationId`: Returns a list of metering points included in a specific customer authorization.
            
`customerCVR`: Returns a list of metering points for which access has been granted by a specific customer
  (based on the CVR of the customer/granting party).
            
`customerKey`: Returns a list of metering points linked to a specific customer key.
  The customer key can be supplied by the third party during the process of granting data access.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Define what kind of authorization id to filter on. Possible values are: 'authorizationId', 'customerCVR', 'customerKey'

401.description: When the provided token doesn't meet the requirements

This request is used for retrieving a list of metering point IDs for which access has been granted.
A filter value must be supplied to limit the result.
            
The following filter options are available:
`authorizationId`: Returns a list of metering point IDs included in a specific customer authorization.
            
`customerCVR`: Returns a list of metering point IDs for which access has been granted by a specific customer
  (based on the CVR of the customer/granting party).
            
`customerKey`: Returns a list of metering point IDs linked to a specific customer key.
  The customer key can be supplied by the third party during the process of granting access.

get.description:
This request is used for retrieving details about authorizations (powers of attorney) granted by customers.
            
Only data regarding valid or active authorizations is returned.
Data related to deleted or expired authorizations is not included in the response.

401.description: When the provided token dont meet the requirements

get.description:
Call this endpoint to verify whether we are currently operating normally.
            
If we are experiencing more traffic than we can handle, this endpoint may return HTTP 503.
The status currently refreshes every 60 seconds.

post.description:
This request is used for querying time series data for one or more metering points
for which access has been granted, for a specified period and with a specified aggregation level.
            
Please note that it is only possible to retrieve time series data for the previous five years plus the current year.
By default, only the latest complete access period for each metering point is queried. If multiple historical
access periods are enabled by the deployment, the response can contain repeated metering point IDs.
            
Possible request-level error codes:
            
- `20013`: The request does not contain any valid metering point IDs.
- `30000`: `dateFrom` is later than today.
- `30001`: `dateFrom` is later than `dateTo`.
- `30002`: `dateFrom` and `dateTo` are equal.
- `30003`: `dateTo` is later than tomorrow.
- `30004`: `dateFrom` or `dateTo` is not a valid date.
- `30008`: The requested aggregation is not supported.
- `30017`: `dateTo` is on or before the earliest supported date.
            
A successful HTTP 200 response contains one result per metering point. An individual result can contain
`20003` or `20004` (invalid metering point ID), `20008` (metering point not found), `20010` (relation not found),
`20011` (an unexpected error occurred), `30010` (the requested period is not covered by an authorization),
`30014` (the effective end date is not later than the start date, for example when `dateFrom` is today and `dateTo` is tomorrow because future end dates are adjusted to today),
`30015` (no data available), `30016` (relation expired),
`30018` (the entire requested period is outside the metering point's available-data period, or `dateFrom` is before the metering point was registered in DataHub),
or `40014` (no authorization found).

400.description: One or more request parameters are missing or invalid, such as the date range, aggregation, or metering point list.

401.description: If you do not have access

post.description:
This request is used for querying details (master data) for one or more metering points (for which access has been granted).
By default, master data is queried using the latest complete access period for each metering point. A deployment
can enable canonical multiple-period behavior for compatibility.

401.description: If you do not have access to one or more of the listed metering point id(s)

post.description:
This request is used for querying charge data—such as subscriptions and tariffs—for one or more metering points
for which access has been granted.
            
Charges linked to the metering point at the time of the request or on any future date will be returned.
            
However, past and future changes to an existing charge are not included in the response.

401.description: If you do not have access to one or more of the listed metering point id(s)

post.description:
This request is used for querying charge links, charge information, and charge series for one or more
metering points and date intervals for which access has been granted.

401.description: If you do not have access to one or more of the listed metering point id(s)

404.description: When the Charges integration feature is disabled

get.description:
In order to get an access token you will need
a valid refresh token. This token can be fetched from the portal.
The token is a JWT token. There are tools that can read the content eg: https://jwt.io/
The token must be submittet in the request header like "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOi..."

403.description: When a non-refresh token is used

401.description: When the provided token don't meet the requirements

If the customer has granted several authorizations with different includeFutureMeteringPoints values, then the value of most recent active authorization takes precedence

name.description: Unique metering point id consisting of 18 characters.

meteringPointId.description: Unique metering point id consisting of 18 characters

parentMeteringPointId.description: The id of the related parent metering point. Only applicable for child metering points

typeOfMP.description:
Specifies the type of metering point.
            
Possible values:
            
D01 (VE Production), D02 (Analysis), D04 (Surplus production group 6), D05 (Net production),
D06 (Supply to grid), D07 (Consumption from grid), D08 (Wholesale services), D09 (Own production),
D10 (Net from grid), D11 (Net to grid), D12 (Total consumption), D14 (Electrical heating),
D15 (Net consumption), D17 (Other consumption), D18 (Other production), D19 (Capacity Settlement), D99 (Internal use),
E17 (Consumption measurement point), E18 (Production measurement point).

energyTimeSeriesMeasureUnit.description:
Specifies the energy measurement unit relevant for the metering point.
            
Possible values:
            
AMP (Ampere), H87 (Count/Quantity), K3 (kVArh - KiloVolt-Ampere reactive hour),
KWH (kWh - Kilowatt-hour), KWT (kW - Kilowatt), MAW (MW - Megawatt),
MWH (MWh - Megawatt-hour), TNE (Tonne - metric ton), Z03 (MVAr - MegaVolt-Ampere reactive power),
Z14 (Danish Tariff Code).

estimatedAnnualVolume.description:
Estimated annual consumption/production of the metering
point. Only required for profiled settled metering points. May
exist for metering points with other settlement methods, but is
not necessarily maintained and should therefore not be used.

settlementMethod.description:
Settlement method of the metering point.
            
Possible values:
            
D01 (Flex settled), E01 (Profiled settled), E02 (Non-profiled settled).
            
If a metering point is flex settled or non-profiled settled or has
no settlement method, only non-profiled energy quantities are
registered for the metering point.
If a metering point is profiled settled, profiled energy quantities
(consumption statements) as well as non-profiled energy quantities can be registered for the metering point depending on
the meter reading occurrence (see further details in the section
regarding meterReadingOccurrence elsewhere in this table).
Profiled settled metering points no longer exist, since all profiled settled metering points were converted to flex settled metering points before 01-01-2021.
However, if a metering point used to be profiled settled, profiled energy quantities will still
be registered for the metering point in the period when the
metering point was profiled settled.

meterNumber.description: Meter number identifying the physical meter. Only available if the metering point has a physical meter.

meteringGridAreaIdentification.description: Id of the grid area to which the metering point belongs.

netSettlementGroup.description:
Net settlement group to which the metering point belongs.
            
Possible values:
            
0 (No Net Settlement), 1 (Net Settlement Group 1), 2 (Net Settlement Group 2),
3 (Net Settlement Group 3), 4 (Net Settlement Group 4), 5 (Net Settlement Group 5),
6 (Net Settlement Group 6), 7 (Net Settlement Group 7), 99 (Net Settlement Group 99).

physicalStatusOfMP.description:
Physical status of the metering point.
            
Possible values:
            
D03 (New), E22 (Connected), E23 (Disconnected).

consumerCategory.description: Applies to all consumption metering points. Specifies the threedigit consumer category for the electricityconsumption category which applies to the metering point.

powerLimitKW.description: Specifies the actual maximum limit for power (in kW).

powerLimitKWDecimal.description: Specifies the actual maximum limit for power (in kW) in decimal.

powerLimitA.description: Specifies the actual maximum limit for current (in ampere)

subTypeOfMP.description:
Specifies the sub type of the metering point.
            
Possibles values:
            
D01 (Physical - metering point has a physical meter),
D02 (Virtual - energy volume calculated by grid operator),
D03 (Calculated - energy volume calculated in DataHub).

productionObligation.description: Specifies for a production metering point that a production obligation applies to the metering point and that no change of supplier or move-in/move-out can be carried out for the metering point.

mpCapacity.description: Specifies the power in kW for the production facility.

mpConnectionType.description:
Specifies the connection type of a metering point for which net settlement is used.
            
Possible values:
            
D01 (Direct connected), D02 (Installation connected).

disconnectionType.description:
Specifies how the metering point can be disconnected by the grid operator.
            
Possible values:
            
D00 (For future usage), D01 (Remote disconnection), D02 (Manual disconnection).

product.description:
Product Id.
            
Possible values:
            
Item5790001330590 (Tariff), Item5790001330606 (Fuel quantity), Item8716867000016 (Active power),
Item8716867000023 (Reactive power), Item8716867000030 (Active energy), Item8716867000047 (Reactive energy).

consumerCVR.description: CVR number of the registered consumer. Only available for metering points registered to business consumers.

dataAccessCVR.description: Additional CVR number of the registered consumer. Only available for metering points registered to business consumers.

consumerStartDate.description: Date when the current consumer was registered to the metering point. Not available for child metering points. The date is expressed in UTC as specified in ISO 8601.

meterReadingOccurrence.description:
Specifies the meter reading resolution.
            
Possibles values:
            
ANDET (Other), P1M (Monthly), PT15M (15 Minutes), PT1H (Hourly).
            
If a metering point has meter reading occurrence = Other, only
profiled energy quantities (consumption statements) can be
registered for the metering point.
If a metering point has meter reading occurrence = P1M or
PT15M, only non-profiled energy quantities can be registered
for the metering point.
If a metering point has meter reading occurrence = PT1H, profiled energy quantities (consumption statements) as well as
non-profiled energy quantities can be registered for the metering point depending on the settlement method (see further details elsewhere in this table).
See further details regarding profiled energy quantities versus
non-profiled energy quantities in the sec

mpReadingCharacteristics.description:
Specifies how the metering point is read. Only applicable for profiled metering points.
            
Possible values:
            
D01 (Automatic meter reading), D02 (Manual meter reading).

meterCounterDigits.description: Number of digits on the counting mechanism of a meter. Only applicable for metering points with a physical meter.

meterCounterMultiplyFactor.description: The conversion factor on the counting mechanism of the meter. Only applicable for metering points with a physical meter.

meterCounterUnit.description:
Unit in which the counting mechanism of a meter meters the
energy consumption. Only applicable for metering points with a
physical meter.

meterCounterType.description:
Specifies whether the counter of a meter accumulates or balances consumption. Only applicable for metering points with a physical meter.
            
Possible values:
            
D01 (Accumulated), D02 (Balanced).

taxReduction.description: Specifies whether the consumer is entitled to a potential electricity tax reduction due to electric heating.

taxSettlementDate.description:
The date specifies either the commencement or termination of
an electricity tax reduction. The date is expressed in UTC as
specified in ISO 8601.

mpRelationType.description: Not used. No value is retuned. Will be removed in a later version of the API.

EIC: The Energy Identification Coding (https://www.entsoe.eu/data/energy-identification-codes-eic/)

assetType.description:
Energy type.
            
Possible values:
            
D01 (Steam backpressure turbine), D02 (Gas turbine), D03 (Combined cycle),
D04 (Internal combustion engine Gas), D05 (Steam turbine condensation/steam), D06 (Boiler),
D07 (Stirling engine), D08 (Permanently connected electrical energy storage facilities),
D09 (Temporarily connected electrical energy storage facilities), D10 (Fuel cells),
D11 (Photovoltaics), D12 (Wind turbines), D13 (Hydropower), D14 (Wave power),
D15 (Mixed production), D16 (Production with electrical energy storage facilities),
D17 (Power-to-X), D18 (Regenerative demand facility), D19 (Internal combustion engine diesel engine),
D20 (Biocombustion engine), D99 (Unknown technology).

Specifies if the address can be washed against the public Danish address register.
            
Possible values:
            
D01 (Washable), D02 (Not washable).

mRID.description:
Identification of the market document. If several MarketDocument structures are contained in the same
message, then all of them will have the same id.

createdDateTime.description: The date and time of the creation of the document/message. The date/time is expressed in UTC as specified in ISO 8601.

success.description: True if the request succeded, False if not

errorText.description: Human readable description of the error

id.description: Used to map requests to responses. Ex: data is requested for 10 metering points. The 'Id' will be the requested metering point id for which the reponse belong.

MyEnergyDataMarketDocumentResponseListAp.description: Used as the 'root' class for all responses returned from the public API's. We need these to have a 'root' when the result is transformed to XML

resolution.description:
Specifies the resolution that the specific period covers.
            
Possible values:
            
PT15M (Quarter of an hour), PT1H (Hour), P1D (Day), P1M (Month), P1Y (Year),
PXD (X days - where X is a variable for profiled energy quantities covering various period lengths).

start.description: Start date of period. The date is expressed in UTC as specified in ISO 8601.

end.description: End date of period. The date is expressed in UTC as specified in ISO 8601.

out_Quantity.quantity.description: The quantity value associated with a given point, with a maximum 3 decimals

out_Quantity.quality.description:
The quality of the quantity associated with a given point.
            
Possible values:
            
A01 (Adjusted - will no longer be used after February 2020, specifies energy quantities calculated by DataHub),
A02 (Not available - grid operator submitted missing indicator, no quantity returned),
A03 (Estimated - quantity submitted as estimate by grid operator),
A04 (As provided/Measured - quantity submitted as measured by grid operator),
A05 (Incomplete - aggregated quantity where at least one component has missing indicator).

StringApiResponse.description: Used as the 'root' class for all responses returned from the public API's. We need these to have a 'root' when the result is transformed to XML

StringListApiResponse.description: Used as the 'root' class for all responses returned from the public API's. We need these to have a 'root' when the result is transformed to XML

mRID.description: Unique metering point id consisting of 18 characters.

businessType.description:
A code specifying the nature of the time series.
            
Possible values:
            
A01 (Production), A04 (Consumption), A64 (Consumption - profiled).

curveType.description:
The coded representation of the type of curve being
described. Will always be A01, specifying that the curve
is made of successive Intervals of time (blocks) of constant duration (size), where the size of the blocks is
equal to the resolution of the period.

measurement_Unit.name.description: The unit of measure that is applied to a quantity.

Bearer.description: JWT Authorization header using the Bearer scheme. Example: "Authorization: Bearer {token}"
